results.name: single_example_same_last_digit_far
results.description: Yes-rate for single-example sets on targets >=20 away sharing the example's last digit; observed above null means the model under-produces digit generalisation from one example.

# name: single_example_same_last_digit_far
# description: Yes-rate for single-example sets on targets >=20 away sharing the example's last digit; observed above null means the model under-produces digit generalisation from one example.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    x = ex[:, 0]
    m = (n == 1) & (np.abs(t - x) >= 20) & (np.mod(t, 10) == np.mod(x, 10))
    return rate(m)

results.name: single_example_near_far_gradient
results.description: Single-example sets: yes-rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes-rate for targets >30 away; observed above null means people's similarity gradient is steeper than the model's.

    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)

results.name: wide_vs_narrow_span_fill
results.description: Multi-example sets: yes-rate for targets inside [min,max] when span>=40 minus when span<=15; observed below null means people fill wide spans less than the model predicts.

# name: wide_vs_narrow_span_fill
# description: Multi-example sets: yes-rate for targets inside [min,max] when span>=40 minus when span<=15; observed below null means people fill wide spans less than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    inside = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi) & (n >= 2)
    span = hi - lo
    return rate(inside & (span >= 40)) - rate(inside & (span <= 15))

results.name: arithmetic_rule_outside_boost
results.description: Sets of >=2 all-even examples: yes-rate for even minus odd targets outside the example range; observed above null means people use parity rules more than the model.

# name: arithmetic_rule_outside_boost
# description: Sets of >=2 all-even examples: yes-rate for even minus odd targets outside the example range; observed above null means people use parity rules more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    alleven = np.all(np.mod(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=2.0), 2) == 0, axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    out = alleven & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    return rate(out & (np.mod(t, 2) == 0)) - rate(out & (np.mod(t, 2) == 1))

def test_statistic(df):

    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)

    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)

    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()

results.name: round_target_bias
results.description: Among sets with no multiple-of-10 example, yes-rate for multiple-of-10 targets minus other targets outside the example range; observed above null means people over-accept round numbers relative to the model.
results.code:
# name: round_target_bias
# description: Among sets with no multiple-of-10 example, yes-rate for multiple-of-10 targets minus other targets outside the example range; observed above null means people over-accept round numbers relative to the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    has10 = np.any(np.mod(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=1.0), 10) == 0, axis=1)
    out = (~has10) & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    return rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) == 0)) - rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) != 0))

results.name: shared_last_digit_multi_boost
results.description: Sets where all (>=2) examples share a last digit: yes-rate for outside-range targets with that digit minus other outside-range targets; observed vs null tells whether the model over- or under-produces noticed-digit rules.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_multi_boost
# description: Sets where all (>=2) examples share a last digit: yes-rate for outside-range targets with that digit minus other outside-range targets; observed vs null tells whether the model over- or under-produces noticed-digit rules.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    d = np.mod(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=-1.0), 10)
    d0 = d[:, 0]
    same = (n >= 2) & np.all((d == d0[:, None]) | np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    out = same & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    return rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) == d0)) - rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) != d0))

results.name: upward_vs_downward_extension
results.description: Multi-example sets: yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max minus targets 1-10 below the min; nonzero observed vs null means an asymmetric extension the model misses.

# name: upward_vs_downward_extension
# description: Multi-example sets: yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max minus targets 1-10 below the min; nonzero observed vs null means an asymmetric extension the model misses.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    up = (n >= 2) & (t > hi) & (t <= hi + 10)
    dn = (n >= 2) & (t < lo) & (t >= lo - 10)
    return rate(up) - rate(dn)
